```{r}
#| label: setup
library(ggplot2)
# Ensure UTF-8 so minus signs and ± render in plots on any machine
utf8 <- isTRUE(l10n_info()[["UTF-8"]])   # fall back to ASCII symbols if R is not running in a UTF-8 locale

oi <- c(blue = "#0072B2", orange = "#E69F00", verm = "#D55E00", green = "#009E73",
        sky = "#56B4E9", purple = "#CC79A7", ink = "#1B1F24", grey = "#4A5560")

theme_jc <- theme_minimal(base_size = 17) +
  theme(
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.caption.position = "plot",
    plot.caption = element_text(colour = oi[["grey"]], size = 10.5, hjust = 0),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_text(colour = oi[["ink"]]),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0, colour = oi[["ink"]]),
    legend.position = "top"
  )

src <- "Source: BALANCE Investigators. N Engl J Med 2025;392:1065-78. Recreated from reported data; not the original figure."
umin <- function(x) if (utf8) gsub("-", "\u2212", x, fixed = TRUE) else x
pm <- if (utf8) "\u00b1" else "+/-"
fmt_rd <- function(rd, lo, hi) umin(sprintf("%.1f (%.1f to %.1f)", rd, lo, hi))

# Primary outcome, Table 2 and Figure 2 of the paper
prim <- data.frame(
  analysis = c("Intention-to-treat (primary)", "Per-protocol", "Modified ITT (alive at day 7)"),
  e7  = c(261, 178, 247), n7  = c(1802, 1370, 1788),
  e14 = c(286, 222, 272), n14 = c(1779, 1483, 1765),
  rd  = c(-1.6, -2.0, -1.6), lo = c(-4.0, -4.5, -3.9), hi = c(0.8, 0.6, 0.7),
  ci_level = c("95.7% CI", "95% CI", "95% CI")
)
prim$rd_check <- round(100 * (prim$e7 / prim$n7 - prim$e14 / prim$n14), 1)
stopifnot(all(prim$rd_check == prim$rd))   # counts reproduce the published differences

# Absolute and relative effects, intention-to-treat
r7  <- prim$e7[1] / prim$n7[1]
r14 <- prim$e14[1] / prim$n14[1]
arr <- r14 - r7                      # absolute risk reduction (14 minus 7)
rrr <- arr / r14                     # relative risk reduction
nnt <- 1 / arr                       # point estimate only
# Published 95.7% CI for difference (7 minus 14): -4.0 to 0.8 percentage points
nntb_limit <- 1 / (abs(prim$lo[1]) / 100)   # benefit end of CI
nnth_limit <- 1 / (prim$hi[1] / 100)        # harm end of CI

# Non-inferiority margin in relative terms
margin <- 4
rel_margin_planned  <- margin / 22                 # planning assumption, 22% control mortality
rel_margin_observed <- margin / (100 * r14)        # observed control mortality
```

## Learning objectives {data-budget="1" data-section="Opening"}

By the end of this session you should be able to:

1. Explain how a **non-inferiority** trial differs from a superiority trial
2. Appraise BALANCE with **CONSORT**, **RoB 2** and **GRADE**
3. Decide when **7 days** of antibiotics is reasonable for bacteraemia

::: notes
**Say:** Welcome. Today's paper is a large pragmatic RCT that many of us will meet on the next take. Three objectives: understand non-inferiority, appraise the trial formally, and decide whether it should change what we write on the drug chart.

**Timing:** 1 minute (cumulative 1:00). Press T to start the session timer now.

**Anticipated question:** "Why this paper?" Answer: it applies to almost every specialty that admits patients, the design teaches non-inferiority well, and it is now being cited in local stewardship updates.
:::

## Clinical scenario {data-budget="1.5" data-section="Opening"}

:::: {.card}
**Mrs D, 72.** *E. coli* bacteraemia from pyelonephritis. Admitted to ICU on noradrenaline.

**Day 7:** afebrile for 72 hours, off vasopressors, eating. Switched to an oral agent the isolate is susceptible to.
::::

:::: {.card .orange}
The ward pharmacist asks: **stop today, or complete 14 days?**
::::

::: notes
**Say:** This is a fictional but typical patient. Read the vignette aloud. Ask the room to hold their answer in mind; we will vote on the next slide.

**Timing:** 1.5 minutes (cumulative 2:30).

**Points to draw out:** source is identified and controlled (no obstruction on imaging assumed), organism is not *S. aureus*, she is not severely immunosuppressed and has no prosthetic valve. That places her inside the BALANCE population, which matters later.

**Anticipated question:** "Was the kidney imaged to exclude obstruction or abscess?" Assume yes and no collection. An undrained abscess would have excluded her from BALANCE.
:::

## What would you do? {data-budget="0.5" data-section="Opening"}

```{=html}
<div class="poll">
  <p><strong>Mrs D on day 7. Show of hands, then click to tally.</strong></p>
  <div class="poll-row"><button class="poll-btn">Stop today</button><div class="poll-bar"></div><span class="poll-count">0</span></div>
  <div class="poll-row"><button class="poll-btn">Continue to 10 days</button><div class="poll-bar"></div><span class="poll-count">0</span></div>
  <div class="poll-row"><button class="poll-btn">Complete 14 days</button><div class="poll-bar"></div><span class="poll-count">0</span></div>
</div>
```

::: notes
**Say:** Quick show of hands; click each button once per hand to build the bar chart. We will revisit this vote at the end.

**Timing:** 30 seconds (cumulative 3:00).

**Tip:** if the room is large, estimate in fives and click accordingly. Counts reset when the page reloads.
:::

## Why duration matters {data-budget="1.5" data-section="Background"}

::: {.incremental}
- Bloodstream infection: about **2.9 million deaths** a year worldwide [@balance2025]
- Too short: fear of relapse, failure, selection of resistance
- Too long: adverse events, *C. difficile*, resistance in bystander flora, cost
- Guideline durations varied; **14 days or more** was common in critical illness [@balance2025]
:::

::: notes
**Say:** The authors frame the problem as a balance of harms. Early appropriate therapy improves survival, but nobody had shown that the second week adds anything.

**Timing:** 1.5 minutes (cumulative 4:30).

**Source detail:** the 2.9 million figure and the observation that median durations were 14 days or longer in critically ill patients are from the paper's introduction (its refs 2 and 19).

**Anticipated question:** "Isn't 'complete the course' still the message?" Point out that the 'complete the course' message has been challenged in the UK for some years; the aim is the shortest effective course, which is a question of evidence, not adherence.
:::

## Before BALANCE {data-budget="1.5" data-section="Background"}

| Trial | Patients | Population | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yahav 2019 [@yahav2019] | 604 | Gram-negative, uncomplicated | 7 d non-inferior |
| von Dach 2020 [@vondach2020] | 503 | Gram-negative, uncomplicated | 7 d non-inferior |
| Molina 2022 [@molina2022] | 248 | *Enterobacterales* | 7 d non-inferior |

: Sample sizes as stated in the BALANCE discussion [@balance2025]

Gaps: few ICU patients, gram-negative only, 10-point margins or composite outcomes.

::: notes
**Say:** Three earlier RCTs all favoured seven days, but they were small, restricted to gram-negative organisms, and either excluded ICU patients or enrolled very few. They used wide margins (10 percentage points) or composite outcomes.

**Timing:** 1.5 minutes (cumulative 6:00).

**Anticipated question:** "So why was another trial needed?" Because a 10-point margin for death is very permissive; BALANCE set 4 points and included ICU and gram-positive infections.
:::

## The clinical question (PICO) {data-budget="1" data-section="Background"}

::: {.pico}
::: {.cell}
[P]{.letter} Hospitalised adults, ward or ICU, with a pathogenic bacteraemia; no *S. aureus*, severe immunosuppression or deep focus
:::
::: {.cell}
[I]{.letter} **7 days** of adequate antibiotic therapy
:::
::: {.cell}
[C]{.letter} **14 days** of adequate antibiotic therapy
:::
::: {.cell}
[O]{.letter} Death from any cause by **90 days**; margin 4 percentage points
:::
:::

::: notes
**Say:** Note that 'adequate' means an agent the organism is susceptible to on local laboratory reporting. Drug choice, dose, route and oral switch were left to the treating team. This is a test of a duration strategy, not of a drug.

**Timing:** 1 minute (cumulative 7:00).

**Anticipated question:** "Day 1 counted from when?" Duration was counted as days of adequate treatment; the primary outcome clock started at the date of the index positive blood culture.
:::

## Design and setting {data-budget="1" data-section="Methods"}

- Investigator-initiated, multicentre, **open-label, randomised, non-inferiority** trial
- **74 hospitals, 7 countries**; enrolment October 2014 to May 2023
- Began in ICU only; extended to wards after a parallel ward pilot
- Protocol and statistical analysis plan published before results [@daneman2020protocol]

::: notes
**Say:** Eight and a half years of recruitment, which is itself a teaching point: practice changed over that time (rapid diagnostics, oral step-down).

**Timing:** 1 minute (cumulative 8:00).

**Countries:** the paper lists sites in its Table S1 (supplement), which we did not have. Secondary reports name Australia, Canada, Israel, New Zealand, Saudi Arabia, Switzerland and the USA. [VERIFY against Table S1.] The UK was not a site.

**Anticipated question:** "Who funded it?" Canadian Institutes of Health Research and other public funders in Canada, Australia and New Zealand. All funders listed in the paper are public or charitable research bodies.
:::

## Who could enter? {data-budget="1.5" data-section="Methods"}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Included**

- Admitted when a blood culture grew a pathogenic bacterium
- Ward or ICU
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Excluded**

- *S. aureus* or *S. lugdunensis*; fungaemia
- Severe immunosuppression
- Prosthetic valve or endovascular graft
- Endocarditis, osteomyelitis, septic arthritis, undrained abscess
- Single culture with a likely contaminant
:::
::::

::: notes
**Say:** The exclusions remove exactly the groups where we already treat for longer. Keep this list in mind when we discuss applicability; *S. aureus* is the second most common cause of bacteraemia worldwide according to the authors.

**Timing:** 1.5 minutes (cumulative 9:30).

**Detail:** severe immunosuppression was defined as neutropenia, or immunosuppression after solid organ or haematopoietic stem cell transplant.

**Anticipated question:** "Were coagulase-negative staphylococci excluded?" A single positive culture with a common contaminant was excluded. True CoNS bacteraemia could be included, and CoNS made up 4.8% of isolates.
:::

## Randomisation and intervention {data-budget="1" data-section="Methods"}

- Web-based, variable blocks, 1:1; stratified by **site** and **ICU or ward**
- Allocation **concealed until day 7** of adequate therapy
- Clinicians chose drug, dose, route and oral switch
- Adherence checked daily: assigned duration **±2 days**

::: notes
**Say:** Placebo was not feasible with so many pathogens and regimens. The design compromise is clever: because both arms are identical until day 7, hiding allocation until then removes early differential management.

**Timing:** 1 minute (cumulative 10:30).

**Anticipated question:** "Was outcome assessment blinded?" Mortality is objective. Adjudication of antimicrobial-resistant organisms and all analyses were blinded to group.
:::

## Outcomes and statistics {data-budget="1.5" data-section="Methods"}

- **Primary:** all-cause death by 90 days
- Margin **4 percentage points** (absolute)
- 3626 patients for 80% power, one-sided alpha 2.5%, assuming 22% control mortality
- Three interim analyses, so the primary result uses a **95.7% CI**
- ITT primary; per-protocol and modified ITT as supporting analyses

::: notes
**Say:** A 4-point absolute margin sounds small. In relative terms it is `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * rel_margin_planned)` of the planned 22% control mortality, and `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * rel_margin_observed)` of the observed 14-day mortality of `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * r14)`. Calculated in R from the published figures.

**Timing:** 1.5 minutes (cumulative 12:00).

**Secondary outcomes:** death in hospital and ICU, relapse, adverse events, *C. difficile*, resistant organisms, length of stay, antibiotic-free days and others. No correction for multiplicity; the authors call these exploratory.

**Anticipated question:** "Why both ITT and per-protocol?" In non-inferiority trials ITT can be anti-conservative, so CONSORT asks for both. If they agree, confidence rises.
:::

## Quiz: reading the methods {data-budget="1" data-section="Methods"}

```{=html}
<div class="quiz">
  <div class="q-stem">Why is the primary result reported with a 95.7% rather than a 95% confidence interval?</div>
  <button class="q-opt" data-correct="false">A. The test was one-sided</button>
  <button class="q-opt" data-correct="true">B. Alpha was spent on three interim analyses</button>
  <button class="q-opt" data-correct="false">C. To correct for prespecified subgroups</button>
  <button class="q-opt" data-correct="false">D. To account for clustering by hospital</button>
  <div class="q-explain">The paper states the 95.7% CI reflects the exact alpha spending incurred in the interim analyses. Subgroups and secondary outcomes were not corrected for multiplicity.</div>
  <button class="q-reset">reset</button>
</div>
```

::: notes
**Say:** Give 20 seconds, take a show of hands for each option, then click one to reveal.

**Timing:** 1 minute (cumulative 13:00).

**Follow-up:** clustering by centre was handled in a separate prespecified mixed-model analysis, which gave consistent results.
:::

## Who was randomised? {data-budget="1" data-section="Results"}

```{r}
#| label: plot-flow
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4.6
#| fig-alt: "Horizontal bar chart of trial flow: 36,637 patients with positive blood cultures were assessed, 13,597 were eligible, 3,631 were randomised, 3,608 formed the intention-to-treat population and 3,581 had complete 90-day outcome data."
flow <- data.frame(
  stage = c("Assessed (positive culture)", "Eligible", "Randomised", "Intention-to-treat", "Complete 90-day data"),
  n = c(36637, 13597, 3631, 3608, 3581)
)
flow$stage <- factor(flow$stage, levels = rev(flow$stage))
ggplot(flow, aes(n, stage)) +
  geom_col(fill = oi[["blue"]], width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(aes(label = format(n, big.mark = ",")), hjust = -0.1, size = 6, colour = oi[["ink"]]) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15)), labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(x = "Patients", y = NULL,
       subtitle = "Of 9,966 eligible but not randomised, 4,532 had an attending physician who declined",
       caption = src) +
  theme_jc
```

::: notes
**Say:** Only 26.7% of eligible patients were enrolled. The largest single reason for non-enrolment was the attending physician declining (4,532 patients). That suggests clinicians kept patients they were worried about out of the trial, a selection effect worth discussing.

**Timing:** 1 minute (cumulative 14:00).

**Numbers:** from Figure 1 of the paper. 1,814 assigned 7 days and 1,794 assigned 14 days in the ITT population; 27 lost to follow-up (0.7%).

**Anticipated question:** "Does low enrolment matter if randomisation was sound?" Internal validity is preserved; external validity (who this applies to) is what suffers.
:::

## Baseline characteristics {data-budget="0.5" data-section="Results"}

| Characteristic (n = 3608) | Value |
|---|---|
| Median age | 70 years |
| In ICU at enrolment | 55.0% |
| Community-acquired | 75.4% |
| Urinary source | 42.2% |
| Monomicrobial gram-negative | 71.0% |
| *E. coli* | 43.8% |

: Groups were similar at baseline [@balance2025]

::: notes
**Say:** An older, sick population: more than half in ICU, median SOFA 4. The dominant picture is community-acquired gram-negative urosepsis, which is worth remembering when you generalise.

**Timing:** 30 seconds (cumulative 14:30).

**Extra detail if asked:** intra-abdominal or hepatobiliary 18.8%, lung 13.0%, vascular catheter 6.3%; monomicrobial gram-positive 17.3%, polymicrobial 11.7%; source-control procedure in 44.9%; median Clinical Frailty Scale 4.
:::

## Primary outcome: death by 90 days {data-budget="1.5" data-section="Results"}

```{r}
#| label: plot-primary
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4.4
#| fig-alt: "Forest plot of the risk difference in 90-day mortality, 7 days minus 14 days. Intention-to-treat minus 1.6 percentage points, 95.7% CI minus 4.0 to 0.8. Per-protocol minus 2.0, 95% CI minus 4.5 to 0.6. Modified intention-to-treat minus 1.6, 95% CI minus 3.9 to 0.7. All upper limits lie below the non-inferiority margin of plus 4 points."
pp <- prim
pp$analysis <- factor(pp$analysis, levels = rev(pp$analysis))
pp$lab <- fmt_rd(pp$rd, pp$lo, pp$hi)
ggplot(pp, aes(rd, analysis)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = margin, xmax = 9, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = oi[["orange"]], alpha = 0.18) +
  annotate("text", x = 6.5, y = 3.45, label = "7 days inferior", colour = "#7A5300", size = 5) +
  annotate("text", x = -5.6, y = 3.45, label = "favours 7 days", colour = oi[["grey"]], size = 5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = oi[["grey"]]) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = margin, linetype = "dashed", colour = oi[["verm"]], linewidth = 1) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), width = 0.18, linewidth = 1.1, colour = oi[["blue"]]) +
  geom_point(size = 4.5, shape = 15, colour = oi[["blue"]]) +
  geom_text(aes(x = 9.4, label = lab), hjust = 0, size = 4.6) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-7, 17.5), breaks = seq(-6, 6, 2),
                     labels = function(x) umin(as.character(x))) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(0.6, 0.9))) +
  labs(x = "Risk difference, 7 days minus 14 days (percentage points)", y = NULL,
       subtitle = "Dashed line: non-inferiority margin (+4 points). ITT shows 95.7% CI; other analyses 95% CI", caption = src) +
  theme_jc
```

::: notes
**Say:** 261 of 1,802 died with 7 days (14.5%) and 286 of 1,779 with 14 days (16.1%). Difference −1.6 points, 95.7% CI −4.0 to 0.8. The upper limit is below +4, so non-inferiority is shown. All three analyses agree.

**Timing:** 1.5 minutes (cumulative 16:00).

**Check:** the R code recomputes each difference from the published counts and confirms it matches the published value.

**Anticipated question:** "Does this mean 7 days is better?" No. The interval includes zero, so superiority is not shown. The point estimate favouring 7 days could be chance.
:::

## Absolute effect, calculated {data-budget="1.5" data-section="Results"}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="33%"}
[`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * arr)`]{.big-number}

[ARR, percentage points (point estimate)]{.big-label}
:::
::: {.column width="33%"}
[`r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * rrr)`]{.big-number}

[RRR (point estimate)]{.big-label}
:::
::: {.column width="33%"}
[`r sprintf("%.0f", nnt)`]{.big-number}

[NNT (point estimate)]{.big-label}
:::
::::

:::: {.card .orange}
The CI runs from **NNTB `r sprintf("%.0f", nntb_limit)`** through no effect to **NNTH `r sprintf("%.0f", nnth_limit)`**. An NNT is not meaningful when the CI crosses zero.
::::

::: notes
**Say:** These are calculated in R from the ITT counts (261/1,802 and 286/1,779), not taken from the paper. ARR `r sprintf("%.2f", 100 * arr)` points; RRR `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * rrr)`; NNT `r sprintf("%.1f", nnt)`.

The CI bounds come from inverting the published 95.7% CI limits (−4.0 and +0.8 points). Because the interval crosses zero, the honest expression is 'NNTB `r sprintf("%.0f", nntb_limit)` to infinity to NNTH `r sprintf("%.0f", nnth_limit)`' (Altman's convention).

**Timing:** 1.5 minutes (cumulative 17:30).

**Teaching point:** in a non-inferiority trial the question is not 'how many to treat' but 'how much harm can we exclude'. The data exclude an excess mortality above about 0.8 points with shorter treatment.

**Anticipated question:** "Why not report relative risk?" The trial's margin and analysis were on the absolute scale, which is the scale clinicians and patients use.
:::

## Did patients get what they were assigned? {data-budget="1" data-section="Results"}

```{r}
#| label: plot-adherence
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4.2
#| fig-alt: "Stacked horizontal bars of adherence to assigned duration. 7-day group: 0.8% shorter, 76.1% adherent, 23.1% longer. 14-day group: 5.8% shorter, 83.5% adherent, 10.7% longer."
adh <- data.frame(
  arm = rep(c("Assigned 7 days", "Assigned 14 days"), each = 3),
  cat = rep(c("Shorter than assigned", paste0("Adherent (", pm, "2 days)"), "Longer than assigned"), 2),
  pct = c(0.8, 100 - 23.9, 23.1, 5.8, 100 - 16.5, 10.7)
)
adh$arm <- factor(adh$arm, levels = c("Assigned 14 days", "Assigned 7 days"))
adh$cat <- factor(adh$cat, levels = unique(adh$cat))
ggplot(adh, aes(pct, arm, fill = cat)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(pct > 4, sprintf("%.1f%%", pct), "")),
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), size = 5.5,
            colour = c("white", "white", oi[["ink"]], "white", "white", oi[["ink"]])) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(oi[["purple"]], oi[["blue"]], oi[["orange"]]), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  labs(x = "Patients", y = NULL,
       subtitle = "Median duration received: 8 days (IQR 7 to 11) vs 14 days (IQR 14 to 15)",
       caption = src) +
  theme_jc
```

::: notes
**Say:** Non-adherence was 23.9% in the 7-day arm (almost all longer courses) and 16.5% in the 14-day arm. Clinicians extended treatment when worried, for example persistent sepsis or a new hospital-acquired infection.

**Timing:** 1 minute (cumulative 18:30).

**Anticipated question:** "Does this undermine the result?" It is the key appraisal issue; we return to it in the quiz on non-adherence. Short version: per-protocol and modified ITT analyses agreed, and a later post-hoc analysis adjusting for non-adherence also agreed.
:::

## Subgroups {data-budget="1" data-section="Results"}

```{r}
#| label: plot-subgroups
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5.1
#| fig-alt: "Forest plot of selected prespecified subgroups for 90-day mortality risk difference. Most intervals are wide and several cross the plus 4 point margin, including lung, vascular catheter, unknown source, gram-positive, polymicrobial, Clinical Frailty Scale 5 or more, APACHE II 25 or more and vasopressor use. Gram-negative is minus 2.8, 95% CI minus 5.6 to minus 0.1."
sg <- data.frame(
  group = c(rep("Severity", 5), rep("Source", 5), rep("Pathogen", 3)),
  sub = c("ICU at enrolment", "Ward at enrolment", "APACHE II 25 or more", "Vasopressor or inotrope", "Clinical Frailty Scale 5 or more",
          "Urinary tract", "Intra-abdominal or hepatobiliary", "Lung", "Vascular catheter", "Unknown source",
          "Gram-positive", "Gram-negative", "Polymicrobial"),
  rd = c(-0.3, -3.2, 0.1, 0.5, 2.8, -1.9, -4.2, 1.5, 2.1, 1.2, 1.6, -2.8, 1.5),
  lo = c(-3.7, -6.3, -7.0, -4.0, -2.1, -5.2, -9.9, -6.1, -8.6, -5.5, -4.5, -5.6, -5.8),
  hi = c(3.1, 0.0, 7.2, 5.1, 7.8, 1.4, 1.4, 9.0, 12.7, 7.9, 7.7, -0.1, 8.7)
)
sg$group <- factor(sg$group, levels = c("Severity", "Source", "Pathogen"))
sg$sub <- factor(sg$sub, levels = rev(sg$sub))
sg$crosses <- ifelse(sg$hi >= margin, "Upper limit at or beyond +4", "Upper limit below +4")
ggplot(sg, aes(rd, sub, colour = crosses, shape = crosses)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = oi[["grey"]]) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = margin, linetype = "dashed", colour = oi[["verm"]], linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), width = 0.25, linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 3.2) +
  facet_grid(group ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(oi[["orange"]], oi[["blue"]]), name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(17, 15), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-10, 12, 2), labels = function(x) umin(as.character(x))) +
  labs(x = "Risk difference, 7 minus 14 days (percentage points, 95% CI)", y = NULL, caption = src) +
  theme_jc + theme(legend.position = "top", axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12.5),
                   strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0))
```

::: notes
**Say:** Subgroups are broadly consistent, but many intervals are wide and cross the margin, so we cannot claim non-inferiority within them. The authors say as much. Two to watch: frail patients (CFS 5 or more: +2.8, 95% CI −2.1 to 7.8) and lung source (+1.5, −6.1 to 9.0). These are hypothesis-generating only.

**Timing:** 1 minute (cumulative 19:30).

**Anticipated question:** "Gram-negative looks significantly better with 7 days?" −2.8 (−5.6 to −0.1) just excludes zero, but with 13 or more subgroups and no multiplicity correction, one nominally significant result is expected by chance.

Subgroup values from Figure 3 of the paper; CIs are 95% and unadjusted.
:::

## Secondary outcomes {data-budget="0.5" data-section="Results"}

```{r}
#| label: plot-secondary
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-alt: "Forest plot of binary secondary outcomes, risk difference 7 minus 14 days with 95% CI: death in hospital minus 1.0 (minus 2.9 to 0.9); death in ICU minus 0.6 (minus 3.2 to 1.9); relapse 0.4 (minus 0.6 to 1.4); C. difficile minus 0.2 (minus 1.1 to 0.6); resistant organism colonisation or infection 1.1 (minus 0.8 to 2.9); allergy minus 0.3 (minus 0.9 to 0.3); acute kidney injury minus 0.1 (minus 0.7 to 0.5)."
sec <- data.frame(
  out = c("Death in hospital", "Death in ICU", "Relapse of bacteraemia", "C. difficile infection",
          "Resistant organism (any culture)", "Allergy", "Acute kidney injury"),
  rd = c(-1.0, -0.6, 0.4, -0.2, 1.1, -0.3, -0.1),
  lo = c(-2.9, -3.2, -0.6, -1.1, -0.8, -0.9, -0.7),
  hi = c(0.9, 1.9, 1.4, 0.6, 2.9, 0.3, 0.5)
)
sec$out <- factor(sec$out, levels = rev(sec$out))
sec$lab <- fmt_rd(sec$rd, sec$lo, sec$hi)
ggplot(sec, aes(rd, out)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = oi[["grey"]]) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), width = 0.22, linewidth = 1, colour = oi[["green"]]) +
  geom_point(size = 3.5, shape = 15, colour = oi[["green"]]) +
  geom_text(aes(x = 3.5, label = lab), hjust = 0, size = 4.6) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-3.5, 6.8), breaks = seq(-3, 3, 1), labels = function(x) umin(as.character(x))) +
  labs(x = "Risk difference, 7 minus 14 days (percentage points, 95% CI)", y = NULL,
       subtitle = "Antibiotic-free days by day 28: 19 vs 14, median difference 5 (4.6 to 5.4)",
       caption = src) +
  theme_jc
```

::: notes
**Say:** No detectable differences in relapse, *C. difficile*, allergy, AKI or resistant organisms. But these events were rare, so the intervals are wide relative to the event rates. The clear gain is five more antibiotic-free days by day 28, and one fewer day in hospital (median 10 vs 11; difference −1, 95% CI −1.5 to −0.5).

**Timing:** 30 seconds (cumulative 20:00).

**Anticipated question:** "So shorter courses do not reduce resistance?" The trial could not show it: resistance was measured from routine cultures, not active surveillance, and follow-up for *C. difficile* missed community and readmission episodes, as the authors acknowledge.
:::

## Quiz: interpreting the result {data-budget="1" data-section="Results"}

```{=html}
<div class="quiz">
  <div class="q-stem">ITT difference −1.6 points (95.7% CI −4.0 to 0.8); margin +4. Which statement is correct?</div>
  <button class="q-opt" data-correct="false">A. 7 days is superior to 14 days</button>
  <button class="q-opt" data-correct="true">B. 7 days is non-inferior; superiority is not shown</button>
  <button class="q-opt" data-correct="false">C. Inconclusive, because the CI crosses zero</button>
  <button class="q-opt" data-correct="false">D. 14 days is superior for gram-positive infection</button>
  <div class="q-explain">The upper limit (0.8) lies below the +4 margin, so non-inferiority is shown. The interval includes zero, so superiority is not. Subgroup results are too imprecise to support D.</div>
  <button class="q-reset">reset</button>
</div>
```

::: notes
**Say:** Option C catches people who apply superiority logic to a non-inferiority trial. Crossing zero is expected; the test is whether the interval stays clear of the margin.

**Timing:** 1 minute (cumulative 21:00).
:::

## Authors' conclusions vs our appraisal {data-budget="0.5" data-section="Appraisal"}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.card}
**Authors**

In hospitalised patients with bloodstream infection, "antibiotic treatment for 7 days was noninferior to treatment for 14 days" [@balance2025]
:::
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.card .orange}
**Our appraisal (next slides)**

Agree for the **included** population. Caution where excluded or under-represented.
:::
:::
::::

::: notes
**Say:** Keep these separate. The authors' claim is narrow and matches the data. What follows is our own appraisal, not the authors'.

**Timing:** 30 seconds (cumulative 21:30).
:::

## CONSORT non-inferiority extension {data-budget="1.5" data-section="Appraisal"}

| Item [@piaggio2012] | BALANCE |
|---|---|
| Margin prespecified and justified | Yes: 4 points, tighter than the 10 points used elsewhere |
| Sample size based on margin | Yes: 3626 planned, 3608 analysed |
| ITT **and** per-protocol reported | Yes, both non-inferior |
| CI interpreted against margin | Yes (95.7% CI) |
| Reference treatment proven effective | No: 14 days is custom, not placebo-tested |

::: notes
**Say:** The design is reported well. The last row is the subtle one. Classic non-inferiority logic assumes the comparator has proven efficacy against placebo. Fourteen days has never been shown to beat a shorter course, so the margin is a clinical judgement about acceptable extra deaths, not a fraction of a known treatment effect [@mulla2012].

**Timing:** 1.5 minutes (cumulative 23:00).

**Anticipated question:** "Is 4 points small enough?" It is about a quarter of the observed control mortality in relative terms. Would patients accept up to 4 extra deaths per 100 to gain five antibiotic-free days? This is a good discussion point.
:::

## CASP RCT checklist {data-budget="1.5" data-section="Appraisal"}

| CASP question [@casp2020] | Judgement |
|---|---|
| Focused question; randomised | Yes |
| All patients accounted for | Yes: 99.3% and 99.2% with day-90 data |
| Blinding | Partial: concealed to day 7, open thereafter; analyses blinded |
| Groups similar at baseline | Yes (Table 1) |
| Treated equally apart from intervention | Unclear: co-interventions not reported |
| Important outcomes covered | Mortality yes; function and patient-reported outcomes no |

::: notes
**Say:** Walk through quickly; most answers are yes. The two weaker areas are the open-label period after day 7 and the lack of information on co-interventions and oral switch timing.

**Timing:** 1.5 minutes (cumulative 24:30).

**Anticipated question:** "Could open-label design bias mortality?" Death is objective, so measurement bias is unlikely. The concern is behaviour: clinicians who know the patient will stop at day 7 may look harder for reasons to continue, which feeds the non-adherence issue.
:::

## Risk of bias: RoB 2, 90-day mortality {data-budget="2" data-section="Appraisal"}

| Domain [@sterne2019] | Judgement | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Randomisation | [Low]{.rob .low} | Web-based, concealed, balanced groups |
| Deviations from intended intervention | [Some concerns]{.rob .some} | Open-label after day 7; 23.9% vs 16.5% non-adherence |
| Missing outcome data | [Low]{.rob .low} | 0.7% lost to follow-up |
| Measurement of outcome | [Low]{.rob .low} | All-cause death |
| Selection of reported result | [Low]{.rob .low} | Protocol and SAP published in advance |
| **Overall** | [Some concerns]{.rob .some} | Driven by deviations domain |

::: notes
**Say:** This is our judgement, not the authors'. The only domain with concerns is deviations. For the effect of assignment (ITT), RoB 2 would often rate deviations that reflect usual practice as low risk. We have been stricter because in a non-inferiority trial, deviations that blur the contrast push towards a finding of non-inferiority.

**Timing:** 2 minutes (cumulative 26:30).

**Anticipated question:** "Would you rate it high risk?" No. Non-adherence was moderate, the median durations still separated by six days, and the supporting analyses agreed.
:::

## Quiz: the non-inferiority trap {data-budget="1" data-section="Appraisal"}

```{=html}
<div class="quiz">
  <div class="q-stem">23% of the 7-day group received longer courses. In an ITT analysis of a non-inferiority trial, this tends to:</div>
  <button class="q-opt" data-correct="true">A. Bias towards finding non-inferiority</button>
  <button class="q-opt" data-correct="false">B. Bias towards finding inferiority</button>
  <button class="q-opt" data-correct="false">C. Have no effect, because ITT preserves randomisation</button>
  <button class="q-opt" data-correct="false">D. Raise mortality equally in both groups</button>
  <div class="q-explain">Crossover makes the arms more alike, shrinking any true difference towards zero and so towards non-inferiority. BALANCE's per-protocol and modified ITT analyses agreed, and a post-hoc analysis adjusting for non-adherence reached the same conclusion.</div>
  <button class="q-reset">reset</button>
</div>
```

::: notes
**Say:** In superiority trials, dilution is conservative. In non-inferiority trials it is anti-conservative. That is why per-protocol analyses matter here.

**Post-hoc analysis** [@ong2026]: non-adherence was associated with prognostic factors (more acute illness, non-urinary source, non-*Enterobacterales* organisms). After inverse probability weighting, the per-protocol risk difference was −1.61% (95% CI −4.13 to 0.87) and the as-treated estimate −0.75% (−3.36 to 1.86), still within the 4-point margin. [VERIFY these figures against the Lancet Infect Dis full text; taken from the published abstract.]

**Timing:** 1 minute (cumulative 27:30).
:::

## Certainty of evidence: GRADE {data-budget="1.5" data-section="Appraisal"}

| Outcome [@guyatt2008] | Certainty | Main reason |
|---|---|---|
| 90-day mortality | **High** | Large trial, precise against margin, consistent with earlier RCTs |
| Antibiotic exposure | **High** | Large, objective difference |
| Relapse | **Moderate** | Imprecision: rare events |
| *C. difficile*, resistance | **Low** | Imprecision; under-ascertainment |

Applies to the trial population; downgrade for indirectness outside it.

::: notes
**Say:** Our GRADE judgement for the question 'in patients like those enrolled'. If you apply it to excluded groups (*S. aureus*, neutropenia, deep foci), indirectness would lower certainty sharply, and in truth the trial gives no evidence for them.

**Timing:** 1.5 minutes (cumulative 29:00).

**Note:** the paper includes a meta-analysis with the earlier trials in Supplementary Figure S1, which we have not reviewed. The 'consistent with earlier RCTs' judgement rests on the three trials summarised earlier.

**Anticipated question:** "Why not downgrade mortality for risk of bias?" The deviations concern was judged not serious because sensitivity analyses agreed.
:::

## Applicability to NHS patients {data-budget="2" data-section="Applicability"}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.card .green}
**Likely applies**

- Community-acquired gram-negative bacteraemia, especially urinary
- Ward and ICU patients who are improving
- Source identified and controlled
:::
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.card .red}
**Does not apply**

- *S. aureus*, fungaemia
- Neutropenia, transplant
- Endovascular, bone, joint or undrained foci
:::
:::
::::

No UK sites; frail patients and non-urinary sources less certain.

::: notes
**Say:** Most NHS bacteraemia on the general take looks like the BALANCE population. Uncertainty remains for frail older patients, lung and catheter sources, and gram-positive organisms other than *S. aureus*, where subgroups were small.

**Timing:** 2 minutes (cumulative 31:00).

**Selection:** 4,532 eligible patients were not enrolled because the attending physician declined. Patients who worried clinicians may be under-represented.

**Anticipated question:** "What about oral step-down?" Route was at clinician discretion and the paper does not report the oral switch rate in the main text, so we cannot say how much of the 7 days was oral.
:::

## Current guidance position {data-budget="2" data-section="Applicability"}

- **UKHSA Start Smart then Focus (2023):** review at 48 to 72 hours [@ukhsa2023sstf]
- **NHS England:** gives 7 days for gram-negative bacteraemia with urinary source as an example of a shortened course [@nhse2025watch]
- **NICE NG253 (2025)** covers recognition and early management of sepsis; [no NICE recommendation on bacteraemia duration]{.verify} [@nice2025ng253]
- Local trust guidelines set duration: check yours

::: notes
**Say:** There is no national NICE recommendation on how long to treat bacteraemia [VERIFY: confirm that NG253 sections 1.8 and 1.9 do not set a duration]. National stewardship guidance asks us to review at 48 to 72 hours, and NHS England's stewardship report cites seven days for gram-negative bacteraemia with urinary source as a shortened course trusts have adopted. That document is England-specific; colleagues in Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales should check their regional guidance.

**Timing:** 2 minutes (cumulative 33:00).

**Anticipated question:** "Does BALANCE change S. aureus practice?" No. *S. aureus* was excluded and the authors explicitly say their results do not apply to it.
:::

## Discussion questions {data-budget="5" data-section="Discussion"}

1. Would you stop Mrs D's antibiotics today? What would make you extend?
2. Is a 4-point margin for death acceptable? Who should decide?
3. 4,532 patients were kept out by their consultant. Does that change your view?
4. Fixed 7 days or individualised duration?

::: notes
**Timing:** 5 minutes (cumulative 38:00). Spend about 1 minute on each, keep 1 minute in reserve.

**Prompts:**

1. Revisit the poll. Has anyone moved? Reasons to extend: persistent bacteraemia, undrained focus, new infection, not improving by day 7.
2. Patients may weigh antibiotic side effects and length of stay against a small possible mortality risk differently from clinicians. Who sets the margin: trialists, guideline panels, patients?
3. Physician refusal suggests the sickest or most complex patients were selected out, though more than half of enrolled patients were in ICU.
4. von Dach 2020 tested CRP-guided duration [@vondach2020]. The authors call for research on individualised, potentially shorter courses.

**Anticipated question:** "What about day 7 falling at the weekend?" Practical, and real. Stop dates written on day 1 or 3 avoid weekend drift.
:::

## Take-home messages {data-budget="2" data-section="Close"}

::: {.incremental}
- 7 days was **non-inferior** to 14 days for 90-day death: −1.6 points (95.7% CI −4.0 to 0.8)
- **5 more antibiotic-free days**; harms too rare to compare reliably
- Non-adherence biases towards non-inferiority, but supporting analyses agree
- Not for *S. aureus*, severe immunosuppression or deep foci
:::

:::: {.card .green}
**Bottom line:** for improving inpatients with uncomplicated, non-*S. aureus* bacteraemia, plan 7 days and justify anything longer.
::::

::: notes
**Say:** Read the bottom line slowly. That is our interpretation, not the authors' wording.

**Timing:** 2 minutes (cumulative 40:00). Press R to reset the timer for the next presenter.

**Anticipated question:** "Can I quote this to my consultant?" Quote the trial and its population; check that the patient meets the inclusion criteria and that local guidance agrees.
:::
